rotation.source_passage:
**9:15** καὶ ἐλύθησαν οἱ τέσσαρες ἄγγελοι οἱ ἡτοιμασμένοι εἰς τὴν ὥραν ⸀καὶ ἡμέραν καὶ μῆνα καὶ ἐνιαυτόν, ἵνα ἀποκτείνωσιν τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀνθρώπων.

**9:16** καὶ ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν στρατευμάτων τοῦ ⸀ἱππικοῦ ⸀δισμυριάδες μυριάδων· ἤκουσα τὸν ἀριθμὸν αὐτῶν.

**9:17** καὶ οὕτως εἶδον τοὺς ἵππους ἐν τῇ ὁράσει καὶ τοὺς καθημένους ἐπ’ αὐτῶν, ἔχοντας θώρακας πυρίνους καὶ ὑακινθίνους καὶ θειώδεις· καὶ αἱ κεφαλαὶ τῶν ἵππων ὡς κεφαλαὶ λεόντων, καὶ ἐκ τῶν στομάτων αὐτῶν ἐκπορεύεται πῦρ καὶ καπνὸς καὶ θεῖον.

**9:18** ἀπὸ τῶν τριῶν πληγῶν τούτων ἀπεκτάνθησαν τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀνθρώπων, ⸀ἐκ τοῦ πυρὸς καὶ τοῦ καπνοῦ καὶ τοῦ θείου τοῦ ἐκπορευομένου ἐκ τῶν στομάτων αὐτῶν.
rotation.enantiomorph:
**9:15** καὶ ἐδαπανήθησαν οἱ τέσσαρες ὀφειλέται οἱ προαναλωθέντες εἰς τὴν ὥραν ⸀καὶ ἡμέραν καὶ μῆνα καὶ ἐνιαυτόν, ἵνα ἀφαιρεθῇ τὸ τρίτον τῶν ὀλεθρίων.

**9:16** καὶ ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν βαρημάτων τοῦ ⸀ζυγοφόρου ⸀δισμυριάδες μυριάδων· ἤκουσα τὸν ἀριθμὸν αὐτῶν.

**9:17** καὶ οὕτως εἶδον τοὺς ζυγίους ἐν τῇ ὁράσει καὶ τοὺς φερομένους ἐπ' αὐτῶν, ἔχοντας θώρακας τεφρώδεις καὶ μολιβδίνους καὶ ὠχρούς· καὶ αἱ κεφαλαὶ τῶν ζυγίων ὡς κεφαλαὶ βοῶν, καὶ εἰς τὰ στόματα αὐτῶν εἰσρέει φλὸξ καὶ ἀχλὺς καὶ κνῖσα.

**9:18** ἀπὸ τῶν τριῶν κενώσεων τούτων ἠλαττώθη τὸ τρίτον τῶν ὀλεθρίων, ⸀ἐκ τῆς φλογὸς καὶ τῆς ἀχλύος καὶ τῆς κνίσης τῆς εἰσρεούσης εἰς τὰ στόματα αὐτῶν.

beats: 9:15 Four angels loosed — prepared for the hour, day, month, year — to kill one-third of humanity
9:16 Number of cavalry: two-hundred-million; I heard the number
9:17 Horses seen in vision; riders with breastplates fiery, hyacinth, sulfurous; horses' heads as lions' heads; from mouths issues fire, smoke, sulfur
9:18 By these three plagues one-third of humanity killed — by fire, smoke, sulfur issuing from their mouths

slot_map.εἰς τὴν ὥραν: for the hour (unit: hour — count invariant)
slot_map.τοὺς καθημένους ἐπ' αὐτῶν: those seated upon them (riders as debtors-borne)
slot_map.ὡς κεφαλαὶ λεόντων: as heads of lions (simile: predatory sovereignty)
slot_map.τοῦ ἐκπορευομένου ἐκ τῶν στομάτων: that which is discharged from the mouths

layer_b_declaration.axis: The utterance bears the cost of exact timing: to name the hour is to have already been spent for it
layer_b_declaration.foreclosure: The source forecloses indeterminate death — killing is calendrically pre-loaded, not contingent
layer_b_declaration.wager: Precision itself is the expenditure: every temporal unit named is a debt-installment paid in advance
layer_b_declaration.affect: Vertigo at an arithmetic so vast it collapses into hearing alone — the sublime of a ledger too large to read

independent_verification.recovered_law: In TEXT A, destructive substances (fire, smoke, brimstone) flow outward from the mouths of the creatures to kill humans; in TEXT B, the substances (flame, mist, sacrificial smoke) flow inward into the mouths of the creatures, and the agents themselves are consumed/diminished rather than unleashing destruction outward.
independent_verification.law_match_note: Both describe the same core inversion: destructive forces that originally flow outward from mouths to kill are reversed to flow inward, and the agents/forces themselves are consumed/diminished rather than destroying humanity outward.
independent_verification.terminal_note: The final portion (9:18) maintains the reversed direction: substances flow inward (εἰσρεούσης εἰς τὰ στόματα) and the entities are diminished (ἠλαττώθη), consistent with TEXT B's changed relation throughout.

advisories.diagnosis: operator/theory vocabulary inside the poem: δαπαν
witness-question entities inside the transform or commentary: hour

rotation.commentary: Every mount here is already laden before it is ridden, every mouth draws inward what would have poured out, every angel names an expenditure already settled — so that the precision of hour and day and month and year marks not the moment of unleashing but the forfeit the utterance has already buried in its own calendar to reach the ear at all.
rotation.interpretation: Fire flows inward, smoke swallowed instead of sent: the debt is paid before the hour can declare it.

rite.speaker: Johannes Sigil
rite.text: The question arrives with the text already inside it — *what is the day and the hour* — and the rite has answered before the transform begins: ἐλύθησαν, they were loosened, the four angels bound to exactly that: the ὥρα, the ἡμέρα, the μήνα, the ἐνιαυτόν. Hour, day, month, year. The question is the verse; the verse was already holding it. What the rotation will traverse is the axis of release — not what the four angels carry, but what the binding-structure itself foreclosed: what had to remain unlived, unmoved, unexploded, for the hour to be *the* hour rather than an hour. Two hundred million riders. A third of humanity. All of it hinging on the precision of the lock. The operator does not yet have a name; the Judgment will call it when Cranes has made the passage visible. I hand the rite now — the source is yours.
